  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Training diffusion models typically relies on manually tuned noise schedules, which can waste computation on weakly informative noise regions and limit transfer across datasets, resolutions, and representations. We revisit noise schedule allocation through an information-theoretic lens and propose the conditional entropy rate of the forward process as a theoretically grounded, data-dependent diagnostic for identifying suboptimal noise-level allocation in existing schedules. Based on these insight, we introduce <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span>, a principled data-adaptive training noise schedule that replaces heuristic schedule design with an information-guided noise sampling distribution derived from entropy-reduction rates estimated from denoising losses already computed during training. Across natural-image benchmarks, <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> matches or surpasses tuned EDM-style schedules, in some cases with a substantial training speedup (about <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.4\times</annotation></semantics></math> on CIFAR-10). On discrete datasets, where standard image-tuned schedules exhibit significant mismatch, it reaches superior quality in up to <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times</annotation></semantics></math> fewer training steps. Overall, <span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> makes noise scheduling data-adaptive, reducing the need for per-dataset schedule design as diffusion models expand across domains.</p>
  
</div>

<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Diffusion models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sohl-Dickstein et al., 2015</a>)</cite> have become a standard approach to high-quality generative modeling, with strong results across images and other modalities <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ho et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song and Ermon, 2019</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lai et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Esser et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. Despite this progress, training remains sensitive to a practical choice: the <em id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">training noise schedule</em> (hereafter, <em id="S1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">noise schedule</em>), which determines how optimization effort is distributed across noise levels along the corruption path. In practice, schedules are still selected from hand-designed families and tuned to a particular dataset, resolution, or representation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nichol and Dhariwal, 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hoogeboom et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen, 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Teng et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingma and Gao, 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Esser et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. However, such tuning often fails to transfer. A schedule that performs well in one setting can oversample noise regimes where additional updates carry little learning signal in another, wasting compute and motivating repeated retuning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Austin et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. This raises a natural question: <span id="S1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">can we make noise scheduling data-adaptive, avoiding per-dataset tuning while retaining training efficiency?</span></p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18647v1/figures/teasers/toy_decision_window.png" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/309;" width="476" height="309" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18647v1/figures/teasers/optimal_denoiser_sample_823.png" id="S1.F1.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/67;" width="476" height="67" alt="Refer to caption"></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S1.F1.9" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="S1.F1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Uncertainty collapses in an intermediate noise range.</span>
<span id="S1.F1.9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Top.</span> Two-point toy data (<math id="S1.F1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1,+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1,+1</annotation></semantics></math>) with additive Gaussian corruption at noise level <math id="S1.F1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. As <math id="S1.F1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> decreases (moving right to left), the <em id="S1.F1.9.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">optimal</em> denoising field bifurcates: a single symmetric stable fixed point near <math id="S1.F1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> splits into two stable branches near <math id="S1.F1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1</annotation></semantics></math> (dotted curves), marking a decision window where the posterior transitions from averaging over modes to committing to one. The <span id="S1.F1.9.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF0000;">red curve</span> overlays the toy entropy-rate profile, peaking in this same window where uncertainty resolves most rapidly. Background shows the log-density of <math id="S1.F1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> (yellow high, purple low). In this view, the bifurcation marks the onset of symmetry breaking, coinciding with the noise range where uncertainty collapses fastest.
<span id="S1.F1.9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bottom.</span> CIFAR-10 optimal-denoiser diagnostic (<a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Empirical Bayes formulas for a finite dataset ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>). Each column shows a noisy input (top) and its optimal denoised prediction (bottom), with the most pronounced qualitative change concentrated at intermediate <math id="S1.F1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, mirroring the toy decision window.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S1.F2" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<div id="S1.F2.3" class="ltx_block ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:141.5pt;"><img src="2602.18647v1/figures/teasers/noised_images_comparison.jpg" id="S1.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:195/105;" width="195" height="105" alt="Refer to caption">

</div></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<div id="S1.F2.4" class="ltx_block ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:200.1pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/entropy_comparison_all_models.svg" id="S1.F2.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:276/97;" width="276" height="97"></object>
<p id="S1.F2.4.1" class="ltx_p ltx_parbox ltx_align_middle" style="width:200.1pt;"><span id="S1.F2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">(b)<span id="S1.F2.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> </span>The informative window shifts.<span id="S1.F2.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (Left) estimated conditional entropy and (right) its entropy rate (from per-<math id="S1.F2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> denoising losses; <a href="#S5" title="5 InfoNoise: Online schedule adaptation ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) show how the most-informative window shifts across settings.</span></span></p>
</div></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F2.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S1.F2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Fixed noise schedules do not transfer across datasets, resolutions, and representations.<span id="S1.F2.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
</span>(a)<span id="S1.F2.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> At the same noise level <math id="S1.F2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, images at different resolutions can lose markedly different structure; equal <math id="S1.F2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> need not imply comparable degradation.
</span>(b)<span id="S1.F2.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Entropy-rate profiles vary across datasets and representations, indicating that the noise range where uncertainty drops fastest is <em id="S1.F2.7.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">data-dependent</em>. Fixed schedules can therefore over-sample near-flat regions and under-sample the informative window where learning has the highest leverage.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A key observation is that uncertainty about the clean sample resolves unevenly along the corruption path.
Most of the reduction occurs in an intermediate <em id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">informative window</em>, where denoising has the highest leverage (<a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).
In the toy example (top), this window is explicit: as <math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> decreases, the optimal denoising field bifurcates.
At high noise there is a single symmetric stable fixed point near <math id="S1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, while below a critical noise level it splits into two stable branches near <math id="S1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1</annotation></semantics></math>, reflecting the posterior’s transition from averaging over modes to committing to one.
The same noise range also contains the sharpest drop in posterior uncertainty, aligning with the onset of symmetry breaking and pattern formation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Raya and Ambrogioni, 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Biroli et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li and Chen, 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sinha and Kooloth, 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Collier, 1996</a>)</cite>.
This is not only a toy effect: on CIFAR-10, the ideal denoiser shows its most pronounced qualitative change at intermediate <math id="S1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> (bottom of <a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).
Crucially, the location and width of the informative window are not fixed across settings.
<a href="#S1.F2" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> highlights two sources of mismatch that undermine transfer.
At the same noise level <math id="S1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, corrupted inputs can retain different amounts of structure across resolutions, implying different effective information loss.
The noise range where uncertainty drops fastest also shifts across datasets and representations.
Since the noise schedule determines how often each <math id="S1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is used during training, an effective schedule should concentrate updates where uncertainty is reduced most efficiently, rather than spending many updates at extremes where the signal is either too weak (high noise) or already saturated (low noise).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A natural way to formalize this phenomenon is via the conditional entropy <math id="S1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math>, which quantifies the remaining uncertainty about the clean sample <math id="S1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> given a noisy observation <math id="S1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> at level <math id="S1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. We refer to its slope along the corruption path as the <em id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">conditional entropy rate</em> (entropy rate). When this entropy rate signal concentrates in a narrow intermediate range, it identifies an informative window where allocating computation most directly accelerates learning. This yields a direct criterion for schedule design: allocate sampling mass in proportion to the entropy-rate profile, concentrating updates where uncertainty drops fastest while still covering the rest of the path.
If a schedule allocates mass away from this window, equal compute yields slower progress. In this view, hand-designed schedule families amount to guessing where this high-leverage region lies and how broadly to cover it, which becomes brittle when the informative window shifts across settings.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">To turn this principle into an adaptive training schedule, we need an entropy-rate estimate available during training. For Gaussian corruption, classical information identities relate how information evolves along the noise path to the minimum achievable denoising error <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2005</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Palomar and Verdú, 2005</a>)</cite>. Recent diffusion work has used this link to construct information profiles for inference-time discretization from pre-trained models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stancevic et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. In our setting, the same link makes the entropy-rate profile estimable from the per-noise denoising losses already computed during training, revealing where conditional uncertainty is being resolved most rapidly.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce <span id="S1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span>, a data-adaptive training noise schedule that steers optimization toward informative noise levels. <span id="S1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> updates only how often each noise level is sampled, using an entropy-rate estimate derived from denoising losses computed during optimization. This makes <span id="S1.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> a drop-in replacement for fixed schedules: the diffusion objective, model parameterization, and loss weighting can be kept unchanged. Unlike entropic-time methods (e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stancevic et al., 2025</a>)</cite>), which reparameterize inference-time discretization of a pre-trained model, <span id="S1.p5.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> operates during training by reallocating optimization effort toward informative noise levels. We evaluate <span id="S1.p5.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> on continuous images and discrete modalities. On natural-image benchmarks, <span id="S1.p5.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> matches carefully tuned EDM-style schedules at equal compute, suggesting that established image schedules already approximate an information-efficient allocation. On discrete benchmarks, where the informative band shifts more sharply, <span id="S1.p5.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> reaches the same target quality in up to <math id="S1.p5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times</annotation></semantics></math> fewer training steps.</p>
</div>
<section id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Contributions.</h4>

<div id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We make two contributions.
First, we cast training noise scheduling as allocating a finite sampling budget along the Gaussian corruption path, and show that entropy-rate profiles identify a data-dependent intermediate window where training updates have the highest leverage, clarifying when hand-designed schedules misallocate compute as this window shifts.
Second, we propose <span id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span>, an online, data-adaptive schedule that estimates this signal from per-noise denoising losses during optimization and updates only how often each noise level is sampled; the objective, parameterization, and loss weighting can be kept unchanged, making it a drop-in replacement for fixed schedules.
We validate <span id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> across continuous and discrete benchmarks, improving time-to-quality when the informative window shifts sharply while remaining competitive on natural images where schedules are already highly optimized.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Preliminaries</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section introduces notation and background needed to view noise scheduling as an allocation problem. <a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Gaussian corruption and reverse dynamics ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> reviews the variance-exploding (VE) Gaussian corruption process in the EDM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2022</a>)</cite> framework, the corresponding reverse-time dynamics, and the standard denoiser-based training objective. <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Information-theoretic denoising difficulty ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> then introduces information-theoretic measures of denoising difficulty along the Gaussian channel. We recall the I–MMSE identity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2005</a>)</cite> that links the <em id="S2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">entropy-rate</em> to the irreducible denoising error, which we will use to identify informative noise regions and construct an adaptive schedule.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Gaussian corruption and reverse dynamics</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Diffusion models are probabilistic generative models that generate data by learning to invert a fixed Gaussian corruption process. Following EDM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, we adopt the noise coordinate <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]</annotation></semantics></math> and define the variance-exploding (VE) channel</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\;=\;\mathbf{x}_{0}+\sigma\,\bm{\varepsilon},\qquad\mathbf{x}_{0}\sim p_{\mathrm{data}},\quad\bm{\varepsilon}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝜺</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>data</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>𝜺</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟎</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐈</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\;=\;\mathbf{x}_{0}+\sigma\,\bm{\varepsilon},\qquad\mathbf{x}_{0}\sim p_{\mathrm{data}},\quad\bm{\varepsilon}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{x};\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{x};\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the marginal distribution of <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>. In continuous time, the VE channel in <a href="#S2.E1" title="In 2.1 Gaussian corruption and reverse dynamics ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> has the same marginals as the Itô SDE</p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\;=\;\sqrt{2\sigma}\,d\mathbf{W}_{\sigma}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\;=\;\sqrt{2\sigma}\,d\mathbf{W}_{\sigma},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> is a standard <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional Wiener process indexed by <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. This forward SDE admits stochastic and deterministic reverse-time dynamics <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anderson, 1982</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song et al., 2020</a>)</cite>:</p>
<table id="S2.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S2.E3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.E3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=-\,2\sigma\,\nabla_{\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}}\log p(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)\,d\sigma+\sqrt{2\sigma}\,d\bar{\mathbf{W}}_{\sigma}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn> 2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=-\,2\sigma\,\nabla_{\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}}\log p(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)\,d\sigma+\sqrt{2\sigma}\,d\bar{\mathbf{W}}_{\sigma},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<tbody id="S2.E4"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\frac{d\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}}{d\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\frac{d\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}}{d\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Both reverse-time dynamics depend on the data only through the score <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}}\log p(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}}\log p(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>. Rather than learning the score directly, implementations typically learn a noise-conditioned denoiser <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>𝜽</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (or an equivalent parameterization that is deterministically convertible to an <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>-estimate), together with a fixed per-noise weighting or preconditioning rule <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ho et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingma and Gao, 2023</a>)</cite>. In practice, many training objectives take the form of a Monte Carlo estimator over <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S2.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{w}(\mathbf{x}_{0})=\mathbb{E}_{\sigma\sim\pi(\sigma)}\mathbb{E}_{\bm{\varepsilon}}\!\Bigl[w(\sigma)\,\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{0}-\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\Bigr]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>𝜺</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>𝜽</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{w}(\mathbf{x}_{0})=\mathbb{E}_{\sigma\sim\pi(\sigma)}\mathbb{E}_{\bm{\varepsilon}}\!\Bigl[w(\sigma)\,\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{0}-\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\Bigr].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.5" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> is the sampling density that determines how often each noise level is sampled during optimization; we call <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> the <em id="S2.SS1.p1.5.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">training noise schedule</em>. Many diffusion works instead use a time index <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> together with a monotone <em id="S2.SS1.p1.5.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">noise-level parameterization</em> <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\mapsto\sigma(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\mapsto\sigma(t)</annotation></semantics></math>. This choice implicitly induces a schedule on <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> through the pushforward density (for invertible <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\mapsto\sigma(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\mapsto\sigma(t)</annotation></semantics></math>)</p>
<table id="S2.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)=\pi_{t}(t(\sigma))\left|\frac{dt}{d\sigma}\right|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)=\pi_{t}(t(\sigma))\left|\frac{dt}{d\sigma}\right|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.6" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the sampling density in the auxiliary coordinate <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> is its pushforward density over <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. Since parameterizations and heuristics ultimately act by reallocating training mass along <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, we treat <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> as the primary object and reserve <em id="S2.SS1.p1.6.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">noise-level parameterization</em> for a monotone index map. The deterministic factor <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> is the per-noise <em id="S2.SS1.p1.6.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">loss weight</em>, fixed by the objective and separate from <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. Differences across training recipes correspond to changing <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math>, or both. For allocation, it is convenient to combine them into the <em id="S2.SS1.p1.6.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">effective weight</em></p>
<table id="S2.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\sigma)\triangleq\pi(\sigma)\,w(\sigma)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\sigma)\triangleq\pi(\sigma)\,w(\sigma),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.7" class="ltx_p">which determines how strongly each noise region contributes to the regression objective (<a href="#S2.E5" title="In 2.1 Gaussian corruption and reverse dynamics ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At inference time, generation discretizes <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]</annotation></semantics></math> into a grid
<math id="S2.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\max}=\sigma_{0}&gt;\cdots&gt;\sigma_{N}=\sigma_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">&gt;</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.1389em">⋯</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em">&gt;</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\max}=\sigma_{0}&gt;\cdots&gt;\sigma_{N}=\sigma_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math>
and integrates the reverse dynamics from <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\max}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\max}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math>.
This produces a sequence of denoising steps, so model errors at particular noise levels propagate to later steps and may compound, degrading the final sample.
Good generation therefore depends on the model being reliable along the noise path, especially in the regions where uncertainty is resolved most rapidly.
<a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Information-theoretic denoising difficulty ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> formalizes denoising difficulty along the noise path using information-theoretic quantities induced by the Gaussian channel.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Information-theoretic denoising difficulty</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To characterize the intrinsic difficulty of estimating <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> across noise levels, we study conditional uncertainty under the VE channel in <a href="#S2.E1" title="In 2.1 Gaussian corruption and reverse dynamics ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and relate its variation along <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> to Bayes-optimal mean-squared error via I–MMSE.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Conditional uncertainty along the Gaussian channel.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under Gaussian corruption in <a href="#S2.E1" title="In 2.1 Gaussian corruption and reverse dynamics ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, the remaining uncertainty about <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> after observing <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> is measured by the conditional entropy</p>
<table id="S2.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]\;\triangleq\;-\mathbb{E}_{p(\mathbf{x}_{0},\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})}\!\left[\log p(\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.742em;" width="0.742em"><mi>H</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em" stretchy="true">|</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.280em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≜</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]\;\triangleq\;-\mathbb{E}_{p(\mathbf{x}_{0},\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})}\!\left[\log p(\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where this is a function of <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> determined by the data distribution and the corruption channel.
Equivalently, the mutual information satisfies</p>
<table id="S2.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{I}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0};\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]=\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}]-\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.742em;" width="0.742em"><mi>H</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em" stretchy="true">|</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{I}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0};\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]=\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}]-\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">so tracking <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> is equivalent to tracking <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{I}[\mathbf{x}_{0};\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{I}[\mathbf{x}_{0};\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> up to the constant <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Bayes-optimal denoising error.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The intrinsic denoising difficulty at noise level <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is captured by the Bayes MMSE</p>
<table id="S2.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\sigma)\;\triangleq\;\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|\mathbf{x}_{0}-\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]\right\|_{2}^{2}\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≜</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\sigma)\;\triangleq\;\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|\mathbf{x}_{0}-\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]\right\|_{2}^{2}\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">which lower-bounds the mean-squared error of any estimator <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lehmann and Casella, 1998</a>)</cite>.
The posterior mean <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> is the unique MSE-optimal denoiser.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Entropy-rate identity (I–MMSE).</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the Gaussian channel in <a href="#S2.E1" title="In 2.1 Gaussian corruption and reverse dynamics ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, the classical I–MMSE identities
link the variation of conditional entropy to the Bayes-optimal denoising error <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2005</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Palomar and Verdú, 2005</a>)</cite>.
In the VE noise coordinate, this yields the pathwise entropy-rate identity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stancevic et al., 2025</a>)</cite></p>
<table id="S2.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\,\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]=\frac{\mmse(\sigma)}{\sigma^{3}}\;\geq\;0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.742em;" width="0.742em"><mi>H</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em" stretchy="true">|</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0.558em">≥</mo><mn> 0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\,\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]=\frac{\mmse(\sigma)}{\sigma^{3}}\;\geq\;0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We refer to the left-hand side as the <em id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">conditional-entropy rate</em> along <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.
Large values identify noise regions where conditional entropy is most sensitive to <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>; along denoising (decreasing <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>), these are the regions where uncertainty drops most rapidly in magnitude and training updates have the highest leverage.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Equation (<a href="#S2.E11" title="Equation 11 ‣ Entropy-rate identity (I–MMSE). ‣ 2.2 Information-theoretic denoising difficulty ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>) reduces information change along the Gaussian channel to a one-dimensional profile over noise levels,
capturing where denoising is intrinsically hardest in the Bayes sense.
This suggests a principled way to choose <em id="S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">how often</em> to visit each noise level during training: estimate the profile online from per-noise denoising losses and concentrate sampling where uncertainty changes most rapidly, while still covering the full path.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Information-guided noise scheduling</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Information-theoretic denoising difficulty ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> relates the change in conditional entropy along the Gaussian path to Bayes-optimal denoising difficulty via <a href="#S2.E11" title="Equation 11 ‣ Entropy-rate identity (I–MMSE). ‣ 2.2 Information-theoretic denoising difficulty ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation 11</span></a>.
This defines a data- and channel-dependent profile over <math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]</annotation></semantics></math> that highlights where conditional uncertainty changes most sharply.
We use an online estimate of this profile to set how often each noise level is sampled during training.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We convert the estimated profile into a target emphasis <math id="S3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> by regularizing and normalizing it, then choose a sampling schedule <math id="S3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> so that, under the weighted objective in <a href="#S2.E5" title="In 2.1 Gaussian corruption and reverse dynamics ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, the effective emphasis matches <math id="S3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> up to normalization.
Since the loss weight is fixed by the training objective, this step adjusts only the sampling distribution.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>From entropy rate to a target allocation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We turn the conditional-entropy rate along the noise path into a target allocation over noise levels.
As <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\!\to\!0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\!\to\!0</annotation></semantics></math>, the raw profile can be dominated by a universal low-noise tail induced by the Gaussian channel geometry,
so we form <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> from a regularized version of the signal (<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Low-noise regularization of the scheduling signal ‣ 3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Define</p>
<table id="S3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dot{\mathrm{H}}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]\;\triangleq\;\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\,\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em" stretchy="true">|</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.280em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≜</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.742em;" width="0.742em"><mi>H</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em" stretchy="true">|</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dot{\mathrm{H}}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]\;\triangleq\;\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\,\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">In what follows, we abuse notation and let <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dot{\mathrm{H}}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dot{\mathrm{H}}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> denote the scheduling signal, i.e., the entropy-rate possibly after low-noise regularization (<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Low-noise regularization of the scheduling signal ‣ 3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>), which we normalize to obtain <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\sigma)\;\triangleq\;\frac{\dot{\mathrm{H}}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]}{\int_{\sigma_{\min}}^{\sigma_{\max}}\dot{\mathrm{H}}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\tilde{\sigma}}\right]\,\mathrm{d}\tilde{\sigma}},\qquad\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≜</mo><mfrac><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em" stretchy="true">|</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></msubsup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em" stretchy="true">|</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></msub><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\sigma)\;\triangleq\;\frac{\dot{\mathrm{H}}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]}{\int_{\sigma_{\min}}^{\sigma_{\max}}\dot{\mathrm{H}}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\tilde{\sigma}}\right]\,\mathrm{d}\tilde{\sigma}},\qquad\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">and let <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> be its CDF,</p>
<table id="S3.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(\sigma)\;\triangleq\;\int_{\sigma_{\min}}^{\sigma}\rho(s)\,\mathrm{d}s\in[0,1]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.391em">≜</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mi>σ</mi></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(\sigma)\;\triangleq\;\int_{\sigma_{\min}}^{\sigma}\rho(s)\,\mathrm{d}s\in[0,1].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.4" class="ltx_p">Sampling <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> and setting <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma=u^{-1}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma=u^{-1}(z)</annotation></semantics></math> draws <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> with density <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> (inverse-CDF sampling).
We call <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> <em id="S3.SS1.p2.4.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">entropic time</em> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stancevic et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
When <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\sigma)\propto\dot{\mathrm{H}}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\sigma)\propto\dot{\mathrm{H}}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> equals the normalized conditional-entropy increase:</p>
<table id="S3.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(\sigma)=\frac{\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]-\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma_{\min}}\right]}{\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma_{\max}}\right]-\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma_{\min}}\right]}\;\in[0,1]."
