width="0.742em"><mi>H</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em" stretchy="true">|</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></msub><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.558em">∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(\sigma)=\frac{\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\right]-\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma_{\min}}\right]}{\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma_{\max}}\right]-\mathrm{H}\!\left[\mathbf{x}_{0}\,\middle|\,\mathbf{x}_{\sigma_{\min}}\right]}\;\in[0,1].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.5" class="ltx_p">In practice, we tabulate <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> on a fixed <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>-grid and evaluate <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> by interpolation (<a href="#S3.F3" title="In 3.1 From entropy rate to a target allocation ‣ 3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, left). Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.1 From entropy rate to a target allocation ‣ 3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> illustrates the construction: the entropy-rate profile is normalized into <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (left), and <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> is then translated into an implementable sampling schedule <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> after accounting for the training loss weight <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (right).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/entropic_scheduler_cifar10.svg" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/168;" width="476" height="168"></object></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/entropic_scheduler_dna.svg" id="S3.F3.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/168;" width="476" height="168"></object></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S3.F3.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps" style="font-size:90%;">InfoNoise<span id="S3.F3.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright"> schedule construction (CIFAR-10, DNA).<span id="S3.F3.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
</span>Left: from rate to allocation.<span id="S3.F3.9.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> We estimate the entropy rate signal <math id="S3.F3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dot{\mathrm{H}}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dot{\mathrm{H}}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> and normalize it to a target density <math id="S3.F3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (<span id="S3.F3.9.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#DE8F05;">orange</span>). Its CDF <math id="S3.F3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> defines <em id="S3.F3.9.1.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">entropic time</em>: sampling uniformly in <math id="S3.F3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> concentrates draws in the <math id="S3.F3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> ranges where uncertainty is reduced most rapidly.
</span>Right: realizing <math id="S3.F3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> under weighted training.<span id="S3.F3.9.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> With per-noise loss weights <math id="S3.F3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>, we sample <math id="S3.F3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)\propto\rho(\sigma)/w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)\propto\rho(\sigma)/w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> so that the effective emphasis <math id="S3.F3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> matches <math id="S3.F3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (up to normalization).</span></span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>From a target allocation to a training schedule</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the weighted objective <a href="#S2.E5" title="In 2.1 Gaussian corruption and reverse dynamics ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, sampling <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\sim\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\sim\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> and applying a fixed loss weight <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> induces an <em id="S3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">effective emphasis</em>
<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\sigma)\triangleq\pi(\sigma)w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\sigma)\triangleq\pi(\sigma)w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> along the noise path. To make this emphasis follow the target allocation <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>, we set (assuming <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]</annotation></semantics></math>)</p>
<table id="S3.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)\ \propto\ \frac{\rho(\sigma)}{w(\sigma)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo rspace="0.500em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.778em">∝</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)\ \propto\ \frac{\rho(\sigma)}{w(\sigma)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Then <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\sigma)\propto\rho(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\sigma)\propto\rho(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>, increasing update frequency in the informative region while leaving the loss weighting of the underlying objective unchanged (<a href="#S3.F3" title="In 3.1 From entropy rate to a target allocation ‣ 3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, right). When <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)\equiv 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)\equiv 1</annotation></semantics></math>, this simplifies to <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)=\rho(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)=\rho(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F4" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F4.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S3.F4.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Discrete domains expose schedule mismatch.<span id="S3.F4.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
</span>Left:<span id="S3.F4.8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Offline reference allocation (from a frozen checkpoint) versus the emphasis induced by fixed samplers (EDM log-normal, log-uniform) and by <span id="S3.F4.8.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span>.

</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Low-noise regularization of the scheduling signal</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For continuous-valued data, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> is a differential entropy and its slope can exhibit a universal small-noise scaling as <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
After normalization, this can concentrate <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> near the low-noise boundary and mask the dataset-specific structure we want to track. We regularize the signal before normalization using the smooth gate</p>
<table id="S3.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{c,n}(\sigma)\;\triangleq\;\frac{\sigma^{n}}{\sigma^{n}+c^{n}},\qquad c&gt;0,\;n\geq 2," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≜</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{c,n}(\sigma)\;\triangleq\;\frac{\sigma^{n}}{\sigma^{n}+c^{n}},\qquad c&gt;0,\;n\geq 2,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and form the pre-allocation <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\sigma)\propto\dot{\mathrm{H}}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]\;g_{c,n}(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.280em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\sigma)\propto\dot{\mathrm{H}}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]\;g_{c,n}(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> before normalizing.
The gate is near <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\gg c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≫</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\gg c</annotation></semantics></math> and decays smoothly for <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\ll c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≪</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\ll c</annotation></semantics></math>, suppressing only the extreme low-noise tail while leaving the
mid-noise region essentially unchanged. Unless stated otherwise, we use <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=3</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For discrete endpoints, <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded, but the entropy-rate in the <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate can still exhibit a strong
low-noise scaling; empirically this regime is often well-approximated by a power law over several decades, which we exploit to set the boundary <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>
(see <a href="#S4" title="4 Automatic entropy gating calibration ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Regularization of entropy-rate profiles and pivot selection ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>). We still apply the same gate to the estimated profile so that rare low-<math id="S3.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> spikes do not dominate <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Automatic entropy gating calibration</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The pivot <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> in <a href="#S3.E17" title="In 3.3 Low-noise regularization of the scheduling signal ‣ 3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a> sets where the low-noise gate transitions from suppression to the identity.
We set <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> directly from the current online entropy-rate profile using a method that depends on the endpoint type.
For <span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">continuous endpoints</span>, we use an onset-of-information criterion. The profile is near-zero over much of the high-noise range and becomes appreciable only toward lower noise, so <math id="S4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> marks where uncertainty reduction becomes substantial along the denoising direction.
For <span id="S4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">discrete endpoints</span>, the low-noise region typically exhibits an extended power-law regime in log–log scale (often visible as an approximately flat <math id="S4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(\sigma)\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\sigma)\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>), so we set <math id="S4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> at its departure; details are given in <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Regularization of entropy-rate profiles and pivot selection ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Onset-of-information rule (continuous endpoints).</h4>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(\sigma)\triangleq\dot{\mathrm{H}}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\sigma)\triangleq\dot{\mathrm{H}}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> denote the current ungated entropy-rate profile estimated online (<a href="#S5" title="5 InfoNoise: Online schedule adaptation ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).
We normalize by its peak,</p>
<table id="S4.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{r}(\sigma)\triangleq\frac{r(\sigma)}{\max_{\tilde{\sigma}}r(\tilde{\sigma})}\in[0,1]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{r}(\sigma)\triangleq\frac{r(\sigma)}{\max_{\tilde{\sigma}}r(\tilde{\sigma})}\in[0,1],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">so that <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{r}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{r}=1</annotation></semantics></math> marks the most information-dense regime.
Scanning from high to low noise, we define the onset level as the first persistent crossing of a fixed threshold <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S4.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\;\triangleq\;\sup\Bigl\{\sigma\,\Big|\,\bar{r}(\sigma^{\prime})&lt;p\ \text{for all }\sigma^{\prime}\geq\sigma\Bigr\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0.558em">≜</mo><mrow><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">sup</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" mathsize="1.600em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>for all </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\;\triangleq\;\sup\Bigl\{\sigma\,\Big|\,\bar{r}(\sigma^{\prime})&lt;p\ \text{for all }\sigma^{\prime}\geq\sigma\Bigr\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Thus <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> marks where the entropy-rate becomes appreciable along the denoising direction, and the gate is applied to the low-noise portion <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\leq c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\leq c</annotation></semantics></math>.
We use <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.002" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.002</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.002</annotation></semantics></math> throughout and recompute <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> whenever the schedule is updated. See <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Regularization of entropy-rate profiles and pivot selection ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> for more details.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span><span id="S5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span>: Online schedule adaptation</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S3" title="3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows how the conditional-entropy rate
<math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(\sigma)=\tfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\sigma)=\tfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math>
defines a target allocation and, after accounting for the training loss weight <math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>, a schedule over noise levels.
Since this profile depends on the Bayes MMSE via I–MMSE, it is not available when training from scratch.
<span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> estimates it online from the denoising losses already computed during SGD and periodically rebuilds a <em id="S5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">continuous</em> sampler over <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.
The diffusion objective is unchanged; only the sampling distribution over <math id="S5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is adapted.</p>
</div>

          <span id="alg1.l16.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">    </span><math id="alg1.l16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\pi}\leftarrow\textsc{BuildSampler}\!\left(\{(\sigma_{k},\Delta\sigma_{k},q_{k})\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathsize="0.900em">π</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:6.257em;" width="6.257em"><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps" mathsize="0.900em">BuildSampler</mtext></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">σ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">k</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em" mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">σ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">k</mi></msub></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">q</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">k</mi></msub><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">k</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">K</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\pi}\leftarrow\textsc{BuildSampler}\!\left(\{(\sigma_{k},\Delta\sigma_{k},q_{k})\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg1.l16.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l17" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l17.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">17:</span></span>
            
            
          <span id="alg1.l17.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">   </span><span id="alg1.l17.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">end</span><span id="alg1.l17.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span id="alg1.l17.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">if</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l18" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l18.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">18:</span></span>

</span>

</figure>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Online entropy-rate estimation.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each SGD step produces a pair <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\sigma,\ell)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\sigma,\ell)</annotation></semantics></math> at a sampled (continuous) noise level, and the same loss <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell=\|\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}-\mathbf{x}_{0}\|_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell=\|\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}-\mathbf{x}_{0}\|_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> used for the SGD update is also used for scheduling.
We route <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\sigma,\ell)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\sigma,\ell)</annotation></semantics></math> to its log-grid interval <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and keep a FIFO buffer <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> of recent losses per bin.
At refresh time, we average the buffer to obtain <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\ell}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\ell}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, smooth <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\ell}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\ell}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> across refreshes to obtain a stable per-bin loss estimate <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{\mathrm{mse}}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>mse</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{\mathrm{mse}}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, and then form the entropy-rate estimate via I–MMSE (<a href="#S2.E11" title="Equation 11 ‣ Entropy-rate identity (I–MMSE). ‣ 2.2 Information-theoretic denoising difficulty ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation 11</span></a>),
<math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{r}_{k}=\widehat{\mathrm{mse}}_{k}/\sigma_{k}^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>mse</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{r}_{k}=\widehat{\mathrm{mse}}_{k}/\sigma_{k}^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The grid is used for estimation and numerical integration; sampling remains continuous.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Boundary regularization and pivot calibration.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Raw estimates can concentrate near <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Low-noise regularization of the scheduling signal ‣ 3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>).
At each refresh, we set the pivot <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> from the current profile
(power-law boundary for discrete endpoints; onset-of-information for continuous endpoints; see
<a href="#S4" title="4 Automatic entropy gating calibration ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sections</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Regularization of entropy-rate profiles and pivot selection ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>),
then apply the gate <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{c,n_{\mathrm{gate}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>gate</mi></msub></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{c,n_{\mathrm{gate}}}</annotation></semantics></math> to suppress only the extreme low-noise tail.
Optionally, we apply light smoothing across neighboring grid points on the log-grid to reduce estimator noise without shifting the dominant peak.
We denote the resulting (gated, optionally smoothed) profile by <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{r}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{r}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sampler refresh and continuous realization.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Every <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> optimization steps, once all intervals have at least <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math> samples, we rebuild the sampler.
We convert the gated profile into tabulated density values <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{k}\propto\widetilde{r}_{k}/w(\sigma_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∝</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{k}\propto\widetilde{r}_{k}/w(\sigma_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> so that the effective emphasis <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> follows <a href="#S3" title="3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.
<span id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">BuildSampler</span> normalizes <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{q_{k}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{q_{k}\}</annotation></semantics></math> using <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\sigma_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\sigma_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, builds a continuous CDF by numerical integration over <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, and samples continuous <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> values via inverse-CDF interpolation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Warm-up and stability.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use a fixed baseline sampler <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\mathrm{base}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>base</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\mathrm{base}}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\mathrm{warm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>warm</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\mathrm{warm}}</annotation></semantics></math> steps to populate all intervals.
We also enforce a minimum count <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math> before each refresh, preventing updates driven by under-sampled regions.
The FIFO capacity <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> keeps the estimate responsive as the model changes, while the refresh period <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> controls how often the sampler is rebuilt.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Noise schedules determine how training updates are distributed along the corruption path, and therefore which stages of uncertainty resolution receive compute. Our goal is to test whether allocating updates according to dataset-specific information dynamics improves training efficiency <em id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">without modifying the diffusion objective</em>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We study four questions:</p>
<ol id="S6.I1" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Do image-tuned schedules misallocate compute when transferred to discrete representations?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Can the informative region emerge <em id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">online</em> from the evolving denoiser?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Does entropy-rate adaptation remain competitive on mature image benchmarks with refined hand-tuned schedules?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Can the learned allocation also improve inference-time discretization at fixed NFE?</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Experimental setup.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unless stated otherwise, we fix architecture, optimizer, augmentations, EMA, and training budget, and vary only the sampling distribution <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (hence the realized emphasis <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>).
On continuous images, we keep the EDM objective fixed (including <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{EDM}}(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>EDM</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{EDM}}(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>) and adapt only <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>.
On discrete domains, primary comparisons use <em id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">allocation-controlled</em> training with <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)\equiv 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)\equiv 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so that <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> directly reflects compute allocation.
We additionally report an <em id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">EDM transfer</em> baseline that applies the full EDM recipe (log-normal sampler and <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{EDM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>EDM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{EDM}}</annotation></semantics></math>) without retuning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Compute and metrics.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We measure compute in thousands of processed examples (kEx) and report FID on images <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Heusel et al., 2017</a>)</cite> and Sei-FID on DNA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2022</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Compute-to-target.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>m</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the best score achieved by any fixed baseline within the plotted budget.
We report the first kEx at which each method reaches <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq m^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq m^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>, or the budget limit if unattained.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Offline diagnostics.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Offline diagnostics refer to entropy-rate profiles computed from a frozen, well-trained checkpoint and are used for analysis only. Implementation details are provided in <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Implementation details ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Transfer across representations</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We begin with a controlled test of schedule transfer from continuous images to discrete representations.
<a href="#S3.F4" title="In 3.2 From a target allocation to a training schedule ‣ 3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> compares
(i) an <em id="S6.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">EDM transfer</em> baseline (log-normal sampler + <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{EDM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>EDM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{EDM}}</annotation></semantics></math>),
(ii) a log-uniform sampler under <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w\equiv 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w\equiv 1</annotation></semantics></math>, and
(iii) <span id="S6.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> under <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w\equiv 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w\equiv 1</annotation></semantics></math>.
The left panel overlays the induced emphasis against the offline diagnostic allocation; the right panels report quality versus compute.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/entropy_evolution_DNA.svg" id="S6.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/151;" width="476" height="151"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F5.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S6.F5.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Online schedule emergence on DNA.<span id="S6.F5.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Evolution of the <em id="S6.F5.7.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">training noise schedule</em> <math id="S6.F5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> at several points during training (early<math id="S6.F5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>late), after an initial warm-up under <math id="S6.F5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\mathrm{base}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>base</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\mathrm{base}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The black curve shows the offline diagnostic computed from a frozen, converged checkpoint (analysis-only).
<span id="S6.F5.7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> rapidly concentrates mass in a narrow intermediate-noise band and then changes little, indicating that the informative region is detectable early.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Result.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Across all discrete datasets, the offline diagnostic concentrates mass in a narrow intermediate band, while fixed schedules allocate substantial compute outside this resolving region.
<span id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> shifts probability mass toward the diagnostic band and reaches the best fixed baseline.
<a href="#S6.T1" title="In 6.2 Online emergence of the informative region ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>(a) summarizes final quality and compute-to-target, yielding <math id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.5</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2.8\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.8</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.8\times</annotation></semantics></math> reductions in examples-to-target relative to the best fixed baseline.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We next visualize how this allocation emerges online on DNA sequence in <a href="#S6.SS2" title="6.2 Online emergence of the informative region ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Online emergence of the informative region</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Starting from a short warm-up under a fixed sampler, <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> periodically refreshes <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> using only running denoising-error statistics.
<a href="#S6.F5" title="In 6.1 Transfer across representations ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows that the informative region emerges rapidly and settles early in training.
The emphasis profile stabilizes well before final convergence, suggesting that the informative window is identifiable from intermediate dynamics rather than requiring a fully converged denoiser.</p>
</div>

<div id="S6.T1.4" class="ltx_block ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:113.9pt;">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span><span id="S6.T1.17" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Training efficiency across domains.</span>
<span id="S6.T1.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Discrete domains: final quality and compute-to-target (kEx) under <math id="S6.T1.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w\equiv 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w\equiv 1</annotation></semantics></math> (log-unif, <span id="S6.T1.19" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span>) plus an EDM transfer baseline (EDM sampler + <math id="S6.T1.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{EDM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>EDM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{EDM}}</annotation></semantics></math>).
<span id="S6.T1.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> Continuous images: final FID under the EDM objective; speedup reports the reduction in training compute to reach a fixed FID target (when measured).
“kEx” denotes thousands of processed examples; targets follow <a href="#S3.F4" title="In 3.2 From a target allocation to a training schedule ‣ 3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>Competitive performance on image benchmarks</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate continuous images while keeping the EDM objective fixed and varying only <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Unconditional training efficiency.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On unconditional CIFAR-10, <span id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> reaches the same FID target earlier than the hand-tuned EDM sampler (<a href="#S6.F6" title="In Unconditional training efficiency. ‣ 6.3 Competitive performance on image benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, left), corresponding to a <math id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.4\times</annotation></semantics></math> reduction in training compute.
The learned emphasis concentrates in the same intermediate-noise window identified by EDM, with modest redistribution within that region (<a href="#S6.F6" title="In Unconditional training efficiency. ‣ 6.3 Competitive performance on image benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, right).
Although EDM’s schedule was obtained through extensive empirical tuning, <span id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> recovers the same band directly from online entropy-rate estimation, without manual schedule search.
This agreement suggests that the intermediate-noise window reflects intrinsic information dynamics of the dataset rather than an artifact of heuristic tuning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This pattern holds across continuous datasets: <span id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> matches or slightly improves MNIST and FashionMNIST under identical objectives with comparable or better efficiency, and remains competitive with the tuned EDM schedule on FFHQ <math id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64{\times}64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>64</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64{\times}64</annotation></semantics></math> despite fully automatic adaptation (see <a href="#S6.T1" title="In 6.2 Online emergence of the informative region ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>(b)).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F6" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/cifar10_fid_edm_vs_adaptive_regularized.svg" id="S6.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:234/161;" width="234" height="161"></object></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/loss_vs_sigma_cifar10_065229k.svg" id="S6.F6.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:234/161;" width="234" height="161"></object></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F6.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S6.F6.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Continuous images (EDM objective).<span id="S6.F6.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
</span>Left:<span id="S6.F6.8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Unconditional CIFAR-10 FID versus training compute with identical architecture, optimizer, and objective; only the sampler <math id="S6.F6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> is changed.
</span>Right:<span id="S6.F6.8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The resulting emphasis <math id="S6.F6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)\,w_{\mathrm{EDM}}(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>EDM</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)\,w_{\mathrm{EDM}}(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> along the noise path.
<span id="S6.F6.8.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> concentrates updates in the same intermediate-noise band as EDM’s tuned schedule, while reaching the target FID earlier via small redistributions within that band.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Conditional training efficiency.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On class-conditional CIFAR-10, <span id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> attains the same FID target as the EDM sampler with <math id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.5\times</annotation></semantics></math> fewer processed examples (<a href="#S6.F7" title="In Conditional training efficiency. ‣ 6.3 Competitive performance on image benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>), indicating that the efficiency gains persist under conditioning.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/cifar10_cond_fid_speed.svg" id="S6.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:452/313;" width="452" height="313"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F7.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="S6.F7.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Class-conditional CIFAR-10 training efficiency.<span id="S6.F7.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
FID (<math id="S6.F7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>) versus kimg under the same training recipe and objective, varying only <math id="S6.F7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>.
<span id="S6.F7.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> reaches the EDM target with <math id="S6.F7.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.5\times</annotation></semantics></math> fewer processed examples, showing that the efficiency gains persist under conditioning.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S6.F8" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18647v1/figures/exp/sample_quality_class_6.png" id="S6.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/319;" width="476" height="319" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2602.18647v1/figures/exp/ffhq_edm_info_compare_seed9.png" id="S6.F8.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/318;" width="476" height="318" alt="Refer to caption"></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F8.9" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="S6.F8.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Conditional CIFAR-10 and unconditional FFHQ samples.<span id="S6.F8.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
