(E) EDM training with the standard EDM <math id="S6.F8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>-grid.
(I) <span id="S6.F8.10.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> training with the same EDM grid.
(I+) <span id="S6.F8.10.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> training with an information-guided inference grid (InfoGrid) built from the learned <math id="S6.F8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>.
<span id="S6.F8.10.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> yields cleaner samples; InfoGrid remains stable.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.4 </span>Information-guided discretization for inference</h3>

<figure id="S6.F9" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="S6.F9.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18647v1/figures/samples/generation_path_edm_multi_3images_9steps.png" id="S6.F9.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/161;" width="476" height="161" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F9.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="S6.F9.sf1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">EDM <math id="S6.F9.sf1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>-grid.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="S6.F9.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18647v1/figures/samples/generation_path_info_multi_3images_9steps.png" id="S6.F9.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/161;" width="476" height="161" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F9.sf2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(b)</span> </span><span id="S6.F9.sf2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Uniform-<math id="S6.F9.sf2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> grid (ours).</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="S6.F9.sf3" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/entropy_cdf_rescaled.svg" id="S6.F9.sf3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:450/200;" width="450" height="200"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F9.sf3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(c)</span> </span><span id="S6.F9.sf3.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Linear Path in <span id="S6.F9.sf3.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> space.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="S6.F9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Information-guided discretization for sampling.<span id="S6.F9.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Sample paths from the same initial noise, model, solver (Heun), and NFE.
The only difference is the discretization of <math id="S6.F9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.
(a) The default EDM grid allocates steps unevenly in information space, leading to late-stage noise removal.
(b) Uniform spacing in the learned information coordinate produces more evenly distributed denoising progress.
(c) The cumulative information map <math id="S6.F9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> underlying the grid construction.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next address question (iv): whether the information profile learned during training can also improve inference-time discretization at fixed compute.
<span id="S6.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> estimates an entropy-rate profile <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> along the corruption path, which captures where uncertainty about <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is resolved most rapidly as noise decreases.
Integrating this profile induces a cumulative coordinate over noise levels, and uniform spacing in that coordinate yields a discretization that allocates solver evaluations proportionally to intrinsic information density.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">InfoGrid construction.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given the learned entropy-rate profile <math id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S5" title="5 InfoNoise: Online schedule adaptation ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>), we define the normalized cumulative information coordinate</p>
<table id="S6.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(\sigma)\;\triangleq\;\frac{1}{Z}\int_{\sigma_{\min}}^{\sigma}\tilde{\sigma}\,r(\tilde{\sigma})\,\mathrm{d}\tilde{\sigma},\qquad Z=\int_{\sigma_{\min}}^{\sigma_{\max}}\tilde{\sigma}\,r(\tilde{\sigma})\,\mathrm{d}\tilde{\sigma}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></msubsup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation Z=\int_{\sigma_{\min}}^{\sigma_{\max}}\tilde{\sigma}\,r(\tilde{\sigma})\,\mathrm{d}\tilde{\sigma}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The extra factor <math id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> matches the log-noise measure used in <a href="#S3" title="3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> (equivalently, it corresponds to working in the log-noise parameterization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stancevic et al., 2025</a>)</cite>).
We then choose the inference grid by spacing points uniformly in <math id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> and mapping them back through <math id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.
This yields a non-uniform grid in <math id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> whose steps are (approximately) linear in information space, distributing solver evaluations where uncertainty is actually resolved (<a href="#S6.F9" title="In 6.4 Information-guided discretization for inference ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>(b,c)).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We test this at fixed compute by replacing the hand-designed EDM <math id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>-grid with InfoGrid.
In all comparisons, the model checkpoint, objective, solver (Heun), and number of function evaluations (NFE) are held fixed; only the <math id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> discretization changes.
Figure <a href="#S6.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Conditional training efficiency. ‣ 6.3 Competitive performance on image benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> shows that replacing the EDM grid with InfoGrid yields consistently cleaner or comparable samples at equal NFE.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Straight paths in the appropriate coordinate.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Straightness in <math id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> does not imply uniform information resolution.
Uniform spacing in the learned information coordinate instead produces a trajectory with more evenly distributed uncertainty reduction (<a href="#S6.F9" title="In 6.4 Information-guided discretization for inference ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Taken together, these results show that the informative band can be identified online, improves training efficiency when schedules transfer poorly, remains competitive with tuned image schedules, and also yields an effective inference-time discretization at fixed NFE.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Related work</h2>

<section id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Noise schedules.</h4>

<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The sensitivity of diffusion models to the noise schedule was recognized early in nonequilibrium formulations of generative diffusion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sohl-Dickstein et al., 2015</a>)</cite>.
Early implementations relied on hand-crafted, monotone noise-level parameterizations (e.g., linear variance schedules or log-spaced noise scales) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ho et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song and Ermon, 2019</a>)</cite>.
Later work showed that performance depends on how optimization effort is distributed along the corruption path, motivating shaped schedules (e.g., cosine) and SNR-aware weighting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nichol and Dhariwal, 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingma et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingma and Gao, 2023</a>)</cite>.
A consistent empirical finding is that useful learning signal concentrates in an intermediate noise region: at very high noise, structure is obscured, whereas at very low noise, marginal gains diminish; many heuristics can be read as different ways of emphasizing this regime (cosine/SNR-based weighting, clipping, or logSNR shifts) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hang et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hoogeboom et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen, 2023</a>)</cite>.
EDM makes this allocation explicit via a parametric log-normal sampler over <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, yet scaling and representation changes require retuning its sampler parameters, suggesting that the informative window is representation-dependent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
Related work studies transfer across settings <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Teng et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
Separately, inference-time grids can be designed by controlling discretization error in reverse-time dynamics <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">de Bortoli et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
Flow matching <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lipman et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and rectified-flow scaling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Esser et al., 2024</a>)</cite> likewise rely on time parameterizations and weightings that determine where learning concentrates, and these choices are typically tuned.
In contrast, we cast schedule choice as noise-level allocation and use the conditional entropy-rate to track denoising difficulty in a data-dependent way, guiding allocation during training toward the informative region.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Information theory and diffusion models.</h4>

<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For Gaussian corruption, I–MMSE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2005</a>)</cite> links conditional entropy (and its rate along the noise axis) to Bayes-optimal denoising error, enabling a per-noise notion of denoising difficulty.
This bridge has supported likelihood-related estimators and information-theoretic analyses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kong et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Franzese et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, as well as information-based regularization objectives <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Premkumar, 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
Closest in spirit, entropy-rate signals have been used to reparameterize time so that equal steps correspond to approximately equal information change along the path <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stancevic et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ambrogioni, 2025</a>)</cite>.
However, these uses are primarily analytical, representational, or inference-time.
To our knowledge, prior work has not used the I–MMSE/entropy-rate link as an online training-time control signal to adapt the noise sampling distribution while leaving the underlying objective unchanged.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Diffusion beyond continuous images.</h4>

<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Outside continuous images, corruption geometry and representation shift, so image-tuned schedules need not transfer.
For categorical data, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dieleman et al. (2022)</a></cite> learn a monotone time warp from loss–noise statistics and use inverse-CDF sampling to reshape the training noise distribution; for discrete diffusion, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amin et al. (2025)</a></cite> conditions the reverse model on the jump-time schedule.
<span id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> addresses this by estimating an entropy-rate profile online and reallocating sampling mass accordingly, avoiding hand-designed schedules that assume transfer across representations.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Discussion and conclusions</h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduced <span id="S8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span>, an adaptive noise scheduler that reallocates training updates toward noise levels where uncertainty about the clean sample is reduced most rapidly. The construction follows from the I–MMSE relation for additive Gaussian corruption, which links the slope of the conditional entropy <math id="S8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> to the Bayes-optimal denoising error along the noise path. This yields a dataset- and representation-dependent profile over <math id="S8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> that can be used as a direct allocation signal. This perspective also explains why hand-tuned schedules can be brittle. A schedule tuned on a particular dataset or representation implicitly targets a specific uncertainty-removal geometry along <math id="S8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. When that geometry shifts, the same <math id="S8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> values correspond to a different amount of remaining ambiguity, so updates can be spent in regions that resolve little uncertainty. Our experiments make this mismatch visible when schedules tuned for continuous images are transferred to discrete representations, and show that <span id="S8.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> instead tracks the informative region online without retuning. On image benchmarks where existing schedules are already strong, <span id="S8.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> matches sample quality and can improve training efficiency under the same objective. The same learned information profile can also be reused at inference time to construct grids that take approximately uniform steps in information space, improving discretization at fixed NFE.</p>
</div>
<section id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Limitations.</h4>

<div id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> relies on online, model-dependent estimates of the entropy-rate profile derived from denoising losses, so the signal can be high-variance early in training. In practice, warm-up and low-noise regularization mainly serve to prevent transient misallocation of samples (e.g., brief over-emphasis near <math id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math>), which can waste a small amount of compute rather than affect convergence.
The method also introduces a few scheduler settings (e.g., refresh cadence, buffer/averaging horizon, and gating calibration) that control how quickly the allocation reacts to new evidence versus averaging out noise.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Future work.</h4>

<div id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For continuous data, a key direction is more principled regularization of the low-noise regime that avoids degenerate over-allocation while preserving the informative band. More broadly, the information-allocation view suggests a path toward characterizing schedules that are optimal for a given objective and compute budget, and toward online methods that can track such schedules reliably as training evolves. Extending the same principles beyond Gaussian corruption, and tightening the connection between loss-derived signals and uncertainty reduction in non-Gaussian or discrete mechanisms, are also important directions.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Acknowledgements</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This work was supported by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) as part of the CERTIF-AI project (file number 17998).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="Sx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper advances the methodological foundations of diffusion training by replacing hand-tuned noise schedules with a data-adaptive allocation principle grounded in information dynamics along the corruption path. By reducing trial-and-error schedule design, our approach can lower the compute and engineering burden of deploying diffusion models across new datasets, resolutions, and representations, potentially accelerating research and broadening access. At the same time, improved efficiency can lower the marginal cost of generating high-fidelity synthetic data, amplifying both beneficial uses and harmful misuse.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="Ax1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix" style="font-size:173%;">Appendix</h2>

</section>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> relies on the I–MMSE identity for the additive Gaussian channel <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2005</a>)</cite>, which links Bayes-optimal denoising error to how conditional uncertainty changes along the noise axis.
In particular, the Bayes MMSE <math id="A1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> equals the expected posterior uncertainty under squared loss, and therefore quantifies the irreducible denoising difficulty at noise level <math id="A1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.
For the variance-exploding channel <math id="A1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\sigma}=x_{0}+\sigma\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\sigma}=x_{0}+\sigma\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, this uncertainty controls the conditional-entropy rate:
<math id="A1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\mmse(\sigma)/\sigma^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\mmse(\sigma)/\sigma^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We also analyze a one-dimensional symmetric toy distribution to show explicitly how posterior concentration with decreasing <math id="A1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> yields the “information window” behavior described in the main text.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Gaussian channel, Bayes MMSE, and entropy-rate</h3>

<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Consider the variance-exploding Gaussian channel</p>

<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Bayes denoiser and MMSE (irreducible denoising difficulty).</h4>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Bayes-optimal denoiser under squared loss is the posterior mean</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">For any estimator <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})</annotation></semantics></math> (measurable in <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>),</p>
<table id="A1.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\mathbf{x}_{0}-\hat{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})\|_{2}^{2}\right]\;\geq\;\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\mathbf{x}_{0}-\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)\|_{2}^{2}\right]\;\eqqcolon\;\mmse(\sigma)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo rspace="0.280em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≥</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo rspace="0.280em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≕</mo><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\mathbf{x}_{0}-\hat{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})\|_{2}^{2}\right]\;\geq\;\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\mathbf{x}_{0}-\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)\|_{2}^{2}\right]\;\eqqcolon\;\mmse(\sigma),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(23)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">so <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> is the <em id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">irreducible</em> (Bayes) denoising error at noise level <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.
Equivalently, letting <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)\triangleq\Cov(\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mi>Cov</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)\triangleq\Cov(\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A1.E24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\sigma)=\mathbb{E}_{p(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)}\!\left[\tr\!\left(\Sigma(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)\right)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.670em;" width="0.670em"><mi>tr</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\sigma)=\mathbb{E}_{p(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)}\!\left[\tr\!\left(\Sigma(\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma)\right)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(24)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">I–MMSE and conditional-entropy rates.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma\triangleq\sigma^{-2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>≜</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma\triangleq\sigma^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math> and define the standardized observation</p>
<table id="A1.E25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma}\;\triangleq\;\frac{\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}}{\sigma}=\sqrt{\gamma}\,\mathbf{x}_{0}+\bm{\varepsilon}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>γ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">≜</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mi>σ</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msqrt><mi>γ</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>𝜺</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma}\;\triangleq\;\frac{\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}}{\sigma}=\sqrt{\gamma}\,\mathbf{x}_{0}+\bm{\varepsilon}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">For fixed <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, the map <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\leftrightarrow\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">↔</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>γ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}\leftrightarrow\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math> is bijective, hence
<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(\mathbf{x}_{0};\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})=I(\mathbf{x}_{0};\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>γ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(\mathbf{x}_{0};\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})=I(\mathbf{x}_{0};\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma})</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma]=\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>γ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma};\sigma]=\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma}]</annotation></semantics></math>.
Define
<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\gamma)\triangleq\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\mathbf{x}_{0}-\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma}]\|_{2}^{2}\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>γ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\gamma)\triangleq\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\mathbf{x}_{0}-\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma}]\|_{2}^{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math>,
so <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\sigma)=\mmse(\gamma=\sigma^{-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\sigma)=\mmse(\gamma=\sigma^{-2})</annotation></semantics></math>.
The I–MMSE identity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2005</a>)</cite> states</p>
<table id="A1.E26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial}{\partial\gamma}\,I(\mathbf{x}_{0};\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma})=\frac{1}{2}\,\mmse(\gamma)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>γ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial}{\partial\gamma}\,I(\mathbf{x}_{0};\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\gamma})=\frac{1}{2}\,\mmse(\gamma).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Using <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}]-I(\mathbf{x}_{0};\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}]-I(\mathbf{x}_{0};\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=\sigma^{-2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=\sigma^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math> yields</p>
<table id="A1.E27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\,\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\frac{\mmse(\sigma)}{\sigma^{3}}\;\geq\;0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0.558em">≥</mo><mn> 0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\,\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\frac{\mmse(\sigma)}{\sigma^{3}}\;\geq\;0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Equivalently, with log-SNR <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda\triangleq\log\gamma=\log(1/\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda\triangleq\log\gamma=\log(1/\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A1.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\lambda}\,\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\frac{1}{2}\,\gamma\,\mmse(\gamma)=\frac{1}{2}\,\frac{1}{\sigma^{2}}\,\mmse(\sigma)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\lambda}\,\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\frac{1}{2}\,\gamma\,\mmse(\gamma)=\frac{1}{2}\,\frac{1}{\sigma^{2}}\,\mmse(\sigma).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(28)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>

<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Empirical Bayes formulas for a finite dataset</h3>

<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Empirical prior and noisy marginal.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{x_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{x_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>, define the empirical prior</p>
<table id="A1.E29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The marginal under (<a href="#A1.E20" title="Equation 20 ‣ Channel and induced marginals. ‣ A.1 Gaussian channel, Bayes MMSE, and entropy-rate ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a>) is the Gaussian mixture</p>

</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Here and below <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes an observation (a realization of <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Posterior weights and Bayes denoiser.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Bayes’ rule gives a posterior supported on <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{x_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{x_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with weights</p>

movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation <p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The Bayes denoiser is the posterior mean</p>
<table id="A1.E32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E32.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(x;\sigma)=\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}=x;\sigma]=\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_{i}(x;\sigma)\,x_{i}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(x;\sigma)=\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}=x;\sigma]=\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_{i}(x;\sigma)\,x_{i}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(32)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Computing <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(x;\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(x;\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> amounts to evaluating the <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> posterior weights <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{i}(x;\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{i}(x;\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>, making the ideal denoiser tractable on small datasets (or subsets) and an exact reference under the empirical distribution.
As <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> decreases, the weights typically sharpen: at high noise they are diffuse (the estimate averages many plausible candidates), while at low noise they concentrate on a single exemplar (the estimate becomes nearly decisive).
On CIFAR-10, this produces a rapid qualitative shift over an intermediate <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> range rather than a uniform progression across the noise axis; see <a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and the additional examples in <a href="#A3.F12" title="In Appendix C Extended experiments ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>. See <a href="#A4.SS1" title="D.1 Implementation details: empirical Bayes denoiser ‣ Appendix D Implementation details ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a> for the implementation details.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">

</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and its trace equals the conditional MSE:</p>
