<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tr\,\Cov(\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}=x;\sigma)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_{i}(x;\sigma)\,\|x_{i}-\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(x;\sigma)\|_{2}^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo lspace="0.337em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>Cov</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tr\,\Cov(\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}=x;\sigma)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_{i}(x;\sigma)\,\|x_{i}-\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(x;\sigma)\|_{2}^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(34)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Averaging (<a href="#A1.E34" title="Equation 34 ‣ Posterior covariance and MMSE. ‣ A.2 Empirical Bayes formulas for a finite dataset ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">34</span></a>) over <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\sim p(x;\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\sim p(x;\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> recovers <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> in (<a href="#A1.E24" title="Equation 24 ‣ Bayes denoiser and MMSE (irreducible denoising difficulty). ‣ A.1 Gaussian channel, Bayes MMSE, and entropy-rate ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a>), and thus the entropy rate (<a href="#A1.E27" title="Equation 27 ‣ I–MMSE and conditional-entropy rates. ‣ A.1 Gaussian channel, Bayes MMSE, and entropy-rate ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">27</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Log-density, score, and stationary points.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Up to an additive constant independent of <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A1.E35" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E35.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log p(x;\sigma)=-\frac{d}{2}\log(2\pi\sigma^{2})+\log\!\left(\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\exp\!\left(-\frac{\|x-x_{i}\|_{2}^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.146em;" width="1.146em"><mi>log</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.370em;" width="1.370em"><mi>exp</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log p(x;\sigma)=-\frac{d}{2}\log(2\pi\sigma^{2})+\log\!\left(\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\exp\!\left(-\frac{\|x-x_{i}\|_{2}^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(35)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Differentiating yields the score. Writing <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{x}\log p=\nabla_{x}p/p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>x</mi></msub><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{x}\log p=\nabla_{x}p/p</annotation></semantics></math> and differentiating each Gaussian term gives</p>
<table id="A1.E36" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E36.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{x}\log p(x;\sigma)=\frac{1}{\sigma^{2}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_{i}(x;\sigma)\,x_{i}-x\right)=\frac{\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(x;\sigma)-x}{\sigma^{2}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo lspace="0em" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{x}\log p(x;\sigma)=\frac{1}{\sigma^{2}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_{i}(x;\sigma)\,x_{i}-x\right)=\frac{\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(x;\sigma)-x}{\sigma^{2}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(36)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">which is the score–denoiser identity (Tweedie’s formula) specialized to the empirical prior.
Therefore the stationary points of <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log p(\cdot;\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log p(\cdot;\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (equivalently, zeros of the score) satisfy the self-consistency equation</p>
<table id="A1.E37" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E37.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\nabla_{x}\log p(x;\sigma)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(x;\sigma)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_{i}(x;\sigma)\,x_{i}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>x</mi></msub><mi>log</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{x}\log p(x;\sigma)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=\hat{\mathbf{x}}^{\star}(x;\sigma)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_{i}(x;\sigma)\,x_{i}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(37)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Local stability (optional).</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A stationary point <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is a local maximum of <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log p(\cdot;\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log p(\cdot;\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> iff <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{x}^{2}\log p(x^{\star};\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{x}^{2}\log p(x^{\star};\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> is negative definite (in <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d{=}1</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial x^{2}}\log p(x^{\star};\sigma)&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><msup><mo>∂</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial x^{2}}\log p(x^{\star};\sigma)&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math>).
For the Gaussian channel, differentiating (<a href="#A1.E36" title="Equation 36 ‣ Log-density, score, and stationary points. ‣ A.2 Empirical Bayes formulas for a finite dataset ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">36</span></a>) yields</p>
<table id="A1.E38" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E38.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{x}^{2}\log p(x;\sigma)=\frac{1}{\sigma^{4}}\,\Cov(\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}=x;\sigma)-\frac{1}{\sigma^{2}}\mathbf{I}_{d}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>Cov</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{x}^{2}\log p(x;\sigma)=\frac{1}{\sigma^{4}}\,\Cov(\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}=x;\sigma)-\frac{1}{\sigma^{2}}\mathbf{I}_{d},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(38)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">so local maxima require the posterior spread to be small compared to <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We make this explicit in the one-dimensional toy model below.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Symmetry breaking in a one-dimensional diffusion model</h3>

<figure id="A1.F10" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_floatright" style="width:52%;"><img src="2602.18647v1/figures/teasers/toy_decision_window_mmse.png" id="A1.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:248/164;" width="248" height="164" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A1.F10.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="A1.F10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">To complement <a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> (top), we plot the Bayes MMSE <math id="A1.F10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\sigma)=\mathbb{E}[\Var(x_{0}\mid x_{\sigma};\sigma)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="1.110em">mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="1.110em">Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\sigma)=\mathbb{E}[\Var(x_{0}\mid x_{\sigma};\sigma)]</annotation></semantics></math>, which quantifies residual posterior uncertainty and irreducible denoising difficulty.
Via I–MMSE, <math id="A1.F10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="1.110em">mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> sets <math id="A1.F10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[x_{0}\mid x_{\sigma}]=\mmse(\sigma)/\sigma^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="1.110em">mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[x_{0}\mid x_{\sigma}]=\mmse(\sigma)/\sigma^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The fixed-point branches reveal the symmetry-breaking transition.
The peak in the entropy-rate aligns with this transition, where posterior mass concentrates and information is resolved. Plateaus in the entropy-rate indicate regimes where conditional uncertainty changes little, so samples there resolve minimal new information.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Setup.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Raya and Ambrogioni, 2024</a>)</cite>, we use a one-dimensional toy model to make symmetry breaking analytically transparent. In this setting, the conditional entropy rate provides a direct diagnostic for where posterior uncertainty collapses.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=1</annotation></semantics></math> and consider the symmetric two-point data distribution</p>
<table id="A1.E39" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E39.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{data}}(x_{0})=\frac{1}{2}\delta(x_{0}-a)+\frac{1}{2}\delta(x_{0}+a),\qquad a&gt;0," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>data</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{data}}(x_{0})=\frac{1}{2}\delta(x_{0}-a)+\frac{1}{2}\delta(x_{0}+a),\qquad a&gt;0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A1.F10" title="In A.3 Symmetry breaking in a one-dimensional diffusion model ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> visualizes the induced marginal and the corresponding Bayes denoising field, highlighting the intermediate “decision window” where uncertainty collapses.

</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Posterior weights, denoiser, and posterior variance.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The posterior weight on <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+a</annotation></semantics></math> is</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E41.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{+}(x;\sigma)=\frac{\mathcal{N}(x;a,\sigma^{2})}{\mathcal{N}(x;a,\sigma^{2})+\mathcal{N}(x;-a,\sigma^{2})}=\frac{1}{1+\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{2ax}{\sigma^{2}}\right)},\qquad rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation w_{-}(x;\sigma)=1-w_{+}(x;\sigma),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(41)</span></td></tr></tbody>

<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">so the Bayes denoiser is</p>

<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{0}\in\{\pm a\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo>±</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{0}\in\{\pm a\}</annotation></semantics></math>, the posterior variance is</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E43.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Var(x_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}=x;\sigma)=a^{2}-\hat{x}^{\star}(x;\sigma)^{2}=a^{2}\,\sech^{2}\!\left(\frac{ax}{\sigma^{2}}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msup><mi>sech</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Var(x_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}=x;\sigma)=a^{2}-\hat{x}^{\star}(x;\sigma)^{2}=a^{2}\,\sech^{2}\!\left(\frac{ax}{\sigma^{2}}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
