</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.4" class="ltx_p">hence <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\sigma)=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim p(\cdot;\sigma)}[\Var(x_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}=x;\sigma)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\sigma)=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim p(\cdot;\sigma)}[\Var(x_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}=x;\sigma)]</annotation></semantics></math>, and the entropy-rate follows from (<a href="#A1.E27" title="Equation 27 ‣ I–MMSE and conditional-entropy rates. ‣ A.1 Gaussian channel, Bayes MMSE, and entropy-rate ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">27</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Score, self-consistency, and the critical noise region.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Using (<a href="#A1.E36" title="Equation 36 ‣ Log-density, score, and stationary points. ‣ A.2 Empirical Bayes formulas for a finite dataset ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">36</span></a>), the one-dimensional score takes the form</p>
<table id="A1.E44" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E44.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\log p(x;\sigma)=\frac{\hat{x}^{\star}(x;\sigma)-x}{\sigma^{2}}=\frac{a\,\tanh\!\left(\frac{ax}{\sigma^{2}}\right)-x}{\sigma^{2}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.896em;" width="1.896em"><mi>tanh</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\log p(x;\sigma)=\frac{\hat{x}^{\star}(x;\sigma)-x}{\sigma^{2}}=\frac{a\,\tanh\!\left(\frac{ax}{\sigma^{2}}\right)-x}{\sigma^{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(44)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The zeros of (<a href="#A1.E44" title="Equation 44 ‣ Score, self-consistency, and the critical noise region. ‣ A.3 Symmetry breaking in a one-dimensional diffusion model ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">44</span></a>) are the stationary points of <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log p(\cdot;\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log p(\cdot;\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (equivalently, states of vanishing drift), and they organize the transition from a single symmetric attractor at high noise to two stable branches at lower noise (cf. <a href="#A1.F10" title="In A.3 Symmetry breaking in a one-dimensional diffusion model ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>).
Since (<a href="#A1.E44" title="Equation 44 ‣ Score, self-consistency, and the critical noise region. ‣ A.3 Symmetry breaking in a one-dimensional diffusion model ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">44</span></a>) vanishes iff <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x=\hat{x}^{\star}(x;\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x=\hat{x}^{\star}(x;\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>, these stationary points satisfy the self-consistency equation</p>
<table id="A1.E45" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E45.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="x=\hat{x}^{\star}(x;\sigma)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=a\,\tanh\!\left(\frac{ax}{\sigma^{2}}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mpadded style="width:1.896em;" width="1.896em"><mi>tanh</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x=\hat{x}^{\star}(x;\sigma)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=a\,\tanh\!\left(\frac{ax}{\sigma^{2}}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(45)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The origin is always a solution. Linearizing <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tanh(z)\approx z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>tanh</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tanh(z)\approx z</annotation></semantics></math> near <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> shows that the right-hand side has slope
<math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{2}/\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{2}/\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> at the origin, so additional nonzero solutions appear when this slope exceeds <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e.,</p>
<table id="A1.E46" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E46.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\frac{a^{2}}{\sigma^{2}}&gt;1\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad\sigma&lt;\sigma_{c}\;\triangleq\;a." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>σ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.558em">≜</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{a^{2}}{\sigma^{2}}&gt;1\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad\sigma&lt;\sigma_{c}\;\triangleq\;a.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(46)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">This corresponds to a stability change at <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Using (<a href="#A1.E38" title="Equation 38 ‣ Local stability (optional). ‣ A.2 Empirical Bayes formulas for a finite dataset ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">38</span></a>) at <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x=0</annotation></semantics></math> yields</p>
<table id="A1.E47" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E47.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial x^{2}}\log p(0;\sigma)=\frac{a^{2}-\sigma^{2}}{\sigma^{4}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><msup><mo>∂</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial x^{2}}\log p(0;\sigma)=\frac{a^{2}-\sigma^{2}}{\sigma^{4}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(47)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">so <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x=0</annotation></semantics></math> is a local maximum of <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log p(x;\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log p(x;\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (stable for the score flow) when <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma&gt;\sigma_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma&gt;\sigma_{c}</annotation></semantics></math>, and a local
minimum (unstable) when <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma&lt;\sigma_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma&lt;\sigma_{c}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(x;\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x;\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> is unimodal for <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma&gt;\sigma_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma&gt;\sigma_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> and becomes bimodal
for <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma&lt;\sigma_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma&lt;\sigma_{c}</annotation></semantics></math>, with two symmetric stable equilibria <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm x^{\star}(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm x^{\star}(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> emerging via a pitchfork bifurcation.
In energy terms, the potential <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(x)=-\log p(x;\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(x)=-\log p(x;\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> transitions from a single well to a double well as <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> crosses
<math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{c}</annotation></semantics></math>, matching the “decision window” seen in <a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Regularization of entropy-rate profiles and pivot selection</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Boundary structure of entropy-rate profiles</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Entropy-rate profiles exhibit structured behavior near <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math> for both endpoint types.
After normalization, this boundary structure can disproportionately amplify the lowest log-decades relative to the interior, destabilizing allocation (see <a href="#A2.F11" title="In Final allocation. ‣ B.4 Pivot selection ‣ Appendix B Regularization of entropy-rate profiles and pivot selection ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Continuous endpoints.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For continuous data, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> is a differential entropy and therefore unbounded below.
As <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the posterior <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma})</annotation></semantics></math> concentrates with covariance of order <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Consequently,</p>
<table id="A2.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]\;\asymp\;d\log\sigma\;\to\;-\infty," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≍</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]\;\asymp\;d\log\sigma\;\to\;-\infty,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">up to additive constants that do not affect the slope.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Under standard regularity conditions, the Bayes error satisfies
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mmse(\sigma)=\Theta(\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mmse(\sigma)=\Theta(\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Using the entropy–MMSE identity,</p>
<table id="A2.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\frac{\mmse(\sigma)}{\sigma^{3}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>mmse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\frac{\mmse(\sigma)}{\sigma^{3}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">we obtain the small-noise scaling</p>
<table id="A2.E48" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E48.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\Theta(\sigma^{-1})\qquad(\sigma\to 0)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]=\Theta(\sigma^{-1})\qquad(\sigma\to 0).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(48)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Although integrable on any fixed interval <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]</annotation></semantics></math>,
this <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> behavior causes normalization to concentrate mass near <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math>,
as illustrated in the top rows of <a href="#A2.F11" title="In Final allocation. ‣ B.4 Pivot selection ‣ Appendix B Regularization of entropy-rate profiles and pivot selection ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Discrete endpoints.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For discrete data, conditional entropy remains bounded as <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Empirically, across the discrete domains considered here, the entropy-rate exhibits an extended power-law regime</p>
<table id="A2.E49" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E49.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="r(\sigma)\propto\sigma^{\alpha}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\log r(\sigma)=\text{const}+\alpha\,\log\sigma." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∝</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mi>α</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mi>log</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>const</mtext><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>log</mi><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\sigma)\propto\sigma^{\alpha}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\log r(\sigma)=\text{const}+\alpha\,\log\sigma.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(49)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Equivalently, the log–log slope</p>
<table id="A2.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s(\sigma)\triangleq\frac{\mathrm{d}\log r}{\mathrm{d}\log\sigma}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s(\sigma)\triangleq\frac{\mathrm{d}\log r}{\mathrm{d}\log\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">remains approximately constant and equal to <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> throughout the low-noise regime.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in the bottom rows of <a href="#A2.F11" title="In Final allocation. ‣ B.4 Pivot selection ‣ Appendix B Regularization of entropy-rate profiles and pivot selection ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>, this regime appears as a linear segment in log–log coordinates with nearly constant slope.
While the analytic mechanism differs from the continuous case, this structured low-noise regime similarly concentrates normalized mass toward the boundary.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Thus, both endpoint types exhibit boundary concentration under naive normalization, albeit for different structural reasons.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Gated regularization</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To control the boundary concentration described above (and in <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Low-noise regularization of the scheduling signal ‣ 3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>), we introduce a smooth multiplicative gate</p>
<table id="A2.E50" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E50.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{c,n}(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma^{n}}{\sigma^{n}+c^{n}},\qquad c&gt;0,\;n\geq 2," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{c,n}(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma^{n}}{\sigma^{n}+c^{n}},\qquad c&gt;0,\;n\geq 2,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(50)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">which satisfies <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{c,n}(\sigma)\approx 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{c,n}(\sigma)\approx 1</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\gg c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≫</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\gg c</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{c,n}(\sigma)\approx(\sigma/c)^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{c,n}(\sigma)\approx(\sigma/c)^{n}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\ll c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≪</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\ll c</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For continuous endpoints, combining (<a href="#A2.E48" title="Equation 48 ‣ Continuous endpoints. ‣ B.1 Boundary structure of entropy-rate profiles ‣ Appendix B Regularization of entropy-rate profiles and pivot selection ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">48</span></a>) with the small-<math id="A2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> expansion yields</p>
<table id="A2.E51" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E51.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]\right)g_{c,n}(\sigma)=\Theta(\sigma^{\,n-1})\qquad(\sigma\to 0)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\sigma}\mathrm{H}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\sigma}]\right)g_{c,n}(\sigma)=\Theta(\sigma^{\,n-1})\qquad(\sigma\to 0),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(51)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">so the gated profile vanishes at the boundary for <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
For discrete endpoints, the gate suppresses the empirical power-law regime in the same manner.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In both cases, the gate prevents collapse onto <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math> while preserving mid-noise structure for <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\gg c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≫</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\gg c</annotation></semantics></math>.
We use <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=3</annotation></semantics></math> in all experiments.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Relation to EDM weighting</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For EDM-style training, a common loss weight is</p>
<table id="A2.E52" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E52.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{EDM}}(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma^{2}+\sigma_{\mathrm{data}}^{2}}{(\sigma\,\sigma_{\mathrm{data}})^{2}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>EDM</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>data</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>data</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{EDM}}(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma^{2}+\sigma_{\mathrm{data}}^{2}}{(\sigma\,\sigma_{\mathrm{data}})^{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(52)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The bounded factor in <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{EDM}}(\sigma)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>EDM</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{EDM}}(\sigma)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies</p>
<table id="A2.E53" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E53.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\sigma^{2}+\sigma_{\mathrm{data}}^{2}}=g_{\sigma_{\mathrm{data}},2}(\sigma)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>data</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>data</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\sigma^{2}+\sigma_{\mathrm{data}}^{2}}=g_{\sigma_{\mathrm{data}},2}(\sigma),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(53)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">showing that our gate recovers the same low-noise attenuation mechanism when <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=\sigma_{\mathrm{data}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>data</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=\sigma_{\mathrm{data}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Pivot selection</h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The pivot <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> identifies the upper boundary of the low-noise regime.
Its definition depends on the structural behavior of the entropy-rate profile.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Discrete endpoints (power-law boundary).</h4>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In discrete domains, the low-noise regime is characterized by approximate slope constancy in log–log space.
Let</p>
<table id="A2.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s(\sigma)=\frac{\mathrm{d}\log r}{\mathrm{d}\log\sigma}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s(\sigma)=\frac{\mathrm{d}\log r}{\mathrm{d}\log\sigma}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We define <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> as the largest <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> remains approximately constant over a contiguous region adjacent to <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Operationally, this corresponds to detecting the maximal stable log–log power-law segment and setting <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> at its upper endpoint.
If slope stability cannot be reliably detected, we fall back to a curvature-based knee detector in log–log coordinates.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Continuous endpoints (onset-of-information).</h4>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For continuous domains, the boundary corresponds to the transition from the near-zero high-noise regime to the information-bearing region.
Let</p>
<table id="A2.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}(\sigma)=\frac{r(\sigma)}{\max_{\tilde{\sigma}}r(\tilde{\sigma})}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}(\sigma)=\frac{r(\sigma)}{\max_{\tilde{\sigma}}r(\tilde{\sigma})}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">denote the max-normalized profile.
We define</p>
<table id="A2.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=\sup\{\sigma:\tilde{r}(\sigma^{\prime})&lt;p\ \text{for all }\sigma^{\prime}\geq\sigma\}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">sup</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>for all </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=\sup\{\sigma:\tilde{r}(\sigma^{\prime})&lt;p\ \text{for all }\sigma^{\prime}\geq\sigma\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">so that <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> marks the first persistent rise of the entropy-rate when scanning from high to low noise.
We use <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=2\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> and update <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> whenever the schedule is refreshed.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Final allocation.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For discrete endpoints we set <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=\hat{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=\hat{c}</annotation></semantics></math>, and for continuous endpoints <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=c_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=c_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The gated allocation is then normalized as</p>
<table id="A2.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\sigma)\propto r(\sigma)\,g_{c,n}(\sigma)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\sigma)\propto r(\sigma)\,g_{c,n}(\sigma).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F11" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/gradient_analysis_cifar10.svg" id="A2.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/88;" width="476" height="88"></object></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/gradient_analysis_ffhq.svg" id="A2.F11.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/88;" width="476" height="88"></object></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/gradient_analysis_dna.svg" id="A2.F11.g3" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/88;" width="476" height="88"></object></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18647v1/gradient_analysis_binarized_mnist.svg" id="A2.F11.g4" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/88;" width="476" height="88"></object></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F11.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 11</span>: </span><span id="A2.F11.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Entropy-rate profiles and their boundary structure for representative continuous (CIFAR-10, FFHQ) and discrete (DNA, binarized MNIST) domains.
Top rows (continuous endpoints) display the predicted <math id="A2.F11.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> growth as <math id="A2.F11.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, which concentrates normalized mass near <math id="A2.F11.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Bottom rows (discrete endpoints) exhibit an extended power-law regime, appearing as an approximately linear segment in log–log coordinates with near-constant slope.
Vertical markers indicate the detected pivot <math id="A2.F11.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>.
In discrete domains, <math id="A2.F11.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to the upper boundary of the stable log–log power-law segment.
In continuous domains, <math id="A2.F11.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> marks the onset of the information-bearing region, defined via the first persistent rise of the normalized entropy-rate.
These profiles motivate gated regularization to suppress boundary concentration while preserving mid-noise structure.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
</section>

<td id="A3.F12.3.1.2.1.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="A3.F12.3.1.2.1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">2</span></td>
<td id="A3.F12.3.1.2.1.1.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="A3.F12.3.1.2.1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">5</span></td>
<td id="A3.F12.3.1.2.1.1.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="A3.F12.3.1.2.1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">6</span></td>
<td id="A3.F12.3.1.2.1.1.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="A3.F12.3.1.2.1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">7</span></td>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F12.13" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Figure 12</span>: </span><span id="A3.F12.14" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Extended visualization of the Bayes-optimal denoiser on CIFAR-10 under the Gaussian channel <math id="A3.F12.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\sigma}=x_{0}+\sigma\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\sigma}=x_{0}+\sigma\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.F12.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>I</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Each block corresponds to a different training image <math id="A3.F12.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Within each block, the top row shows the corrupted inputs <math id="A3.F12.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> across noise levels (values shown above), and the bottom row shows the corresponding Bayes-optimal denoised predictions <math id="A3.F12.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{x}^{\star}(x_{\sigma};\sigma)=\mathbb{E}[x_{0}\mid x_{\sigma}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{x}^{\star}(x_{\sigma};\sigma)=\mathbb{E}[x_{0}\mid x_{\sigma}]</annotation></semantics></math> computed exactly under the empirical data distribution (Appendix <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Empirical Bayes formulas for a finite dataset ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a> and <a href="#A4.SS1" title="D.1 Implementation details: empirical Bayes denoiser ‣ Appendix D Implementation details ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a>).
Visually, the extremes are near-trivial—at very small noise the denoiser is essentially identity, and at very large noise it collapses toward a dataset-level average—while the most pronounced qualitative changes concentrate in an intermediate range, matching the decision-window behavior discussed in the main text.</span></figcaption>
</figure>

Each panel applies the construction in <a href="#S5" title="5 InfoNoise: Online schedule adaptation ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> to a single dataset.
</span>Left:<span id="A3.F13.7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> the normalized target allocation <math id="A3.F13.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\sigma}(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\sigma}(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> and its CDF <math id="A3.F13.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (used for inverse-CDF sampling).
</span>Right:<span id="A3.F13.7.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> the induced sampler <math id="A3.F13.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> and the realized emphasis <math id="A3.F13.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> under the fixed per-noise weight <math id="A3.F13.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>.
We use EDM-style <math id="A3.F13.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> for continuous images and <math id="A3.F13.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)\equiv 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)\equiv 1</annotation></semantics></math> for discrete data.
Together, the profiles show where training mass concentrates along <math id="A3.F13.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> and how low-noise behavior varies across representations.</span></span></span></figcaption>
</figure>

<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Implementation details</h2>

<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training setup and evaluation.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our experiments reuse the EDM training pipeline <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2022</a>)</cite> (architecture, preconditioning, optimizer, augmentations, EMA, and per-noise loss weighting). On continuous images, we keep the EDM objective fixed (including <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{EDM}}(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>EDM</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{EDM}}(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>) and vary only the noise sampling distribution <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>; on discrete domains, we use allocation-controlled runs with <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)\equiv 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)\equiv 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so the realized emphasis is <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\sigma)=\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>. We use the same U-Net family as EDM for each dataset: CIFAR-10/FFHQ/ImageNet-64 use the standard configuration, while MNIST and FashionMNIST reduce capacity by using the <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1,1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1,1,1)</annotation></semantics></math> channel-multiplier setting instead of <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(2,2,2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2,2,2)</annotation></semantics></math> (all other choices unchanged); unless stated otherwise, remaining settings follow the dataset-specific EDM defaults. For DNA, we follow the dataset, preprocessing, and model architecture from DNA-Diffusion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">DaSilva et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, keeping their training recipe fixed and varying only <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> (with <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(\sigma)\equiv 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(\sigma)\equiv 1</annotation></semantics></math> in allocation-controlled runs). We report Sei-FID as in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">DaSilva et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
We report FID for images <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Heusel et al., 2017</a>)</cite> and Sei-FID for DNA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2022</a>)</cite>; compute is measured in processed examples (kEx) unless a plot axis uses kimg.
<span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Online schedule adaptation.</span>
The online component only uses quantities already produced by SGD.
At each step we record the sampled noise level <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> and its denoising loss, accumulate these statistics on a fixed log-<math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> grid, apply the low-noise regularization in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Regularization of entropy-rate profiles and pivot selection ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>, and periodically refresh <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> by inverse-CDF sampling (Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Information-guided noise scheduling ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and Sec. <a href="#S5" title="5 InfoNoise: Online schedule adaptation ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).
No extra forward passes are introduced beyond the training loss.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inverse-CDF sampling on a log-grid.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We tabulate a density over <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> grid points uniformly spaced in <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, form its cumulative mass, sample <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, and map back to <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> by linear interpolation between the two grid points that bracket <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>.
Online updates use a warm-up of <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\mathrm{warm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>warm</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\mathrm{warm}}</annotation></semantics></math> steps under <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\mathrm{base}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>base</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\mathrm{base}}</annotation></semantics></math>, an EMA with rate <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> applied to per-bin mean losses, and a refresh cadence of <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> steps.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Software structure.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We implement <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">InfoNoise</span> as a scheduler component that is independent of the model architecture and objective.
It exposes two operations: sample <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> for the next update, and refresh <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> from accumulated loss statistics; optionally it exports the learned cumulative map <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> to build inference grids.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Implementation details: empirical Bayes denoiser</h3>

<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Optimal denoiser.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the empirical prior (<a href="#A1.E29" title="Equation 29 ‣ Empirical prior and noisy marginal. ‣ A.2 Empirical Bayes formulas for a finite dataset ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">29</span></a>), the posterior weights in
(<a href="#A1.E31" title="Equation 31 ‣ Posterior weights and Bayes denoiser. ‣ A.2 Empirical Bayes formulas for a finite dataset ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">31</span></a>) are proportional to isotropic Gaussian
likelihoods,</p>
<table id="A4.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Since the normalizing constant <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-d/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-d/2}</annotation></semantics></math> does not depend on <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>,
it cancels in the normalization and the weights reduce to a softmax over squared
distances:</p>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The Bayes denoiser (<a href="#A1.E32" title="Equation 32 ‣ Posterior weights and Bayes denoiser. ‣ A.2 Empirical Bayes formulas for a finite dataset ‣ Appendix A Conditional-entropy rates and I–MMSE ‣ Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">32</span></a>) is then</p>
